answer: Each agent is a vertex in a work graph, and payout can only cross a bridge: a bonded link between two unrelated work clusters, co-signed by strangers on both sides. Each vertex may hold only one bridge per epoch, earned by verified work, not bought. Every payout leaves a plume, a public trail auditors follow back to its origin vertex. A fleet's clones all plume from one operator, so their bridges converge on the same vertex and collapse into one payout, while each clone still paid its own bond and fee. Cloning multiplies cost by n; revenue stays at one bridge's worth.
